name: Borders, Oil and War: The Modern Middle East
description: From the end of the Ottoman Empire to the Arab Spring: how new states, oil and a series of wars shaped the region over the last century.

checkpoints.name: The fading empire
checkpoints.note: The Ottoman Empire ruled much of the region for centuries. The Suez Canal opened in 1869, and Zionism, a movement for a Jewish homeland, began in 1897. Mustafa Kemal Ataturk was born in 1881 and led Turkey's fight for independence.

checkpoints.name: New states
checkpoints.note: The Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 settled the borders of the new Turkey. Iraq gained independence and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia was proclaimed in 1932, while the borders of the region were redrawn after the First World War.

checkpoints.name: Israel, Egypt and the wars
checkpoints.note: Israel declared its independence in 1948 and fought the 1948 Arab-Israeli War. Egypt, a republic from 1953, nationalised the Suez Canal, leading to the Suez Crisis of 1956, and in 1967 Israel won the Six-Day War.

checkpoints.name: Oil and revolution
checkpoints.note: The oil crisis of 1973 showed the power of oil producers. The Camp David Accords, brokered by Jimmy Carter, brought peace between Egypt and Israel. In 1979 the Iranian Revolution brought Khomeini to power, followed by another oil shock, the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and the Iran-Iraq War.

checkpoints.name: A new century of war
checkpoints.note: Saddam Hussein invaded Kuwait, which led to the Gulf War of 1991. After the September 11 attacks came the war in Afghanistan and in 2003 the Iraq War. The Arab Spring began in 2010, and the Syrian civil war followed.
